parts.title: Campus Conversation: Joining a Photography Club
script: Listen to a conversation between a student and a worker at the student club office.
Hello. I want to join a club. Can you help me?
Sure. What do you like to do?
I like taking photos. Is there a photography club?
Yes, there is. The photo club meets every Tuesday at six o'clock in Room 204.
Great. Do I need a camera?
No. You can use your phone. The club also has three cameras to borrow.
That is good. Is it free?
The club costs ten dollars for the whole year. You can pay here.
OK. I can pay now. Can I come to the meeting next week?
Yes. Next Tuesday, the members will go outside to take photos of the campus. Please bring warm clothes.
Thank you. I am very excited.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the conversation.
OK. I can pay now. Can I come to the meeting next week?
Yes. Next Tuesday, the members will go outside to take photos of the campus. Please bring warm clothes.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: Why Do Leaves Change Color?
script: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Today we will talk about why leaves change color in the fall.
In spring and summer, leaves are green. They have a green material called chlorophyll. Chlorophyll helps the tree make food from sunlight.
In the fall, the days get shorter and the weather gets cold. There is less sunlight, so the tree stops making chlorophyll.
Then the green color goes away. Now we can see other colors in the leaf. These colors were there all summer, but the green hid them.
Yellow and orange colors come from materials called carotenoids. Carotenoids are also the reason carrots are orange.
Some leaves turn red. The red color is made in the fall, when the days are sunny and the nights are cool.
After a few weeks, the leaves turn brown and fall from the tree. The tree rests in winter and grows new leaves in spring.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the lecture.
Yellow and orange colors come from materials called carotenoids. Carotenoids are also the reason carrots are orange.
